newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends down on commission house selling.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends down on commission house selling.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker on light commission house selling, although up from the intra-day lows on consumer hedge buying, traders said.

On the bearish side of the market, London Metal Exchange warehouse stocks jumped another 2,800 tonnes to 237,750 tonnes, but on the bullish side, Falconbridge Ltd's Sudbury mine is in the fourth day of a strike, according to Frederick Demler, minerals economist with ED&F Man.
The active September contract ended at 106.20 cents a lb, down 1.05 cents from Friday's close, while the spot month ended at 106.40 cents a lb, down 0.55 cents.
"The higher stocks was a negative, but Falconbridge was a possible positive," Demler said. "We saw some good consumer buying at the lows. Otherwise it was a pretty quiet session."

Physical traders downplayed the impact of the Falconbridge strike, noting that only the company's copper smelter production is affected. The company's Timmins refinery in Ontario continues to operate.

"It takes a couple of weeks before the refinery production would be affected," said one copper consumer. "If the strike lasts that long, we'll take another look. But for the time being, we're not concerned. There's plenty of copper around."
Sudbury produces 50,000 tonnes of contained copper.
Some physical dealers say demand for copper from the continuous cast copper rod sector is strong, noting that Phelps Dodge has delayed its maintanence shutdown of its Norwich, Connecticut rod mill.

The company declined to comment on the shutdown, but market sources believe the shutdown is scheduled for the last two weeks in September. The shutdown was originally scheduled for the last two weeks of August.
Demand in the other sectors of copper consumption, such as tubing and brass mills, are believed to be suffering through the summer doldrums, traders said.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
